name: Apple Inc.
thesis: Apple trades at $337.82, near its 52-week high of $345.34, with a market cap of ~$4.93 trillion and a trailing P/E of 38.74 versus a forward P/E of 35.25, suggesting the market expects continued earnings growth [1]. Fiscal year 2025 revenue reached $416.16 billion (up 6.43% year-over-year) with net income of $112.01 billion, a net margin of 26.92%, and TTM figures show a gross margin of 48.65% and operating margin of 32.62%, reflecting durable profitability [1]. Free cash flow of $107.72 billion supports a modest dividend yield of 0.32%, though debt-to-equity of 0.7844 indicates meaningful leverage on the balance sheet [1]. Key risks include dependence on global economic conditions, the need to successfully manage frequent product transitions, exposure to adverse legal proceedings and government investigations, volatility in net sales and gross margins, and general stock price volatility (beta of 1.069) [2][1].

risks.text: The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions and adverse economic conditions can materially adversely affect the Company’s business, results of operations, financial condition and stock price.
risks.detail: The Company has international operations with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of the Company’s total net sales. In addition, the Company’s global supply chain is large and complex and a majority of the Company’s supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S. As a result, the Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions.
